text: Got the offer letter this morning. I read it three times in the parking lot and then called Ma before I'd even started the car.
Ravi and I finally fixed the leaking tap ourselves. Took two hours and one YouTube video but we did it and we were ridiculous about how proud we were.
Lena's baby was born at 4am. Both healthy. I cried at the photo and then ate cereal at my desk grinning like an idiot.
Mum sent a voice note singing happy birthday off-key. Played it four times.
Dinner at Noor's. Her mother kept piling food onto my plate and calling me 'beta'. I felt like family.
The landlord agreed to fix the heating AND knocked a bit off the rent for the trouble. I did a little victory lap around the living room.
Coach Ndlovu said I can play in Saturday's match. I've been on the bench all season!
Puppy class graduation. Biscuit did NOT sit on command but he did steal the trainer's hat and everyone clapped anyway.
Results came back: Dr. Okafor says the scan is clear. I sat in the car for ten minutes just breathing and smiling.
Lunch in the sun with Daniela and Chiara, gelato after. Didn't check email for an hour and the world survived.
The plant I thought I'd killed has a new leaf. Hello, little guy.
Leila and I officially ended things. It was kind and mutual and I still cried on the bus home.
Feeling blue. Couldn't tell you why. Ate toast for dinner.
Isabel moved her things out today. The bookshelf looks like a mouth with missing teeth.
First Christmas without Papa. We set his place at the table without saying anything. Nobody could eat much.
Nadia doesn't want to be friends anymore. She said it nicely. I keep rereading the message hoping it says something different.
Mass at the old church for Señora Ruiz. Half the town came. Everyone has a story of her feeding them.
Just a melancholy evening. Old songs, rain, missing people.
Missing the person I was in Lisbon. Free and brave and twenty-three.
First day at the new job on Monday and I keep imagining every way it could go wrong. What if they realise I'm not as good as my interview?
Big party at Hyun's tonight. I want to go. I also want to cancel and stay home where nobody looks at me.
Awake at 3am thinking about climate stuff, the future, whether it's fair to have kids. Big spiral.
Tax deadline is Friday and the shoebox of receipts is still a shoebox.
Hearing that sound again in the walls at night. Probably pipes. I've got the light on anyway.
Bank flagged a weird transaction. Spent an hour on hold. Card's frozen. Still not sure what else they got.
Phone rang from an unknown number three times. I don't pick up unknown numbers. Now I'm convinced something's happened.
Waiting room. Again. Everyone looks as scared as I feel.
Mortgage approval still 'pending'. If it doesn't come through by the 15th we lose the house we've fallen in love with.
Election night. Refreshing the results page like it changes anything. Can't eat.
Walked the dog along the beach at dusk. Just waves and sand and his silly ears flapping. Head clear.
I thought the conversation with Esther would be hard but we listened to each other and I left feeling steady.
Library on a weekday afternoon: old men reading newspapers, a radiator ticking, me and my notebook. Bliss.
Camping. Fire crackling, stars, Rafael asleep in his chair with his mouth open. I feel very still.
Evening walk through the woods with Pablo. The light through the pines was gold. We talked softly about nothing.
Prayer at the temple this morning. Incense, bells, the old priest chanting. I left feeling settled for the whole day.
Painted watercolours on the porch while the cicadas went. Couldn't tell you what time it was.
Night shift was slow. Mopped, restocked, chatted with Ahmed about his allotment. Strangely peaceful at 4am.
Hot springs with Keiko. Steam, snow on the rocks, my whole body went soft.
Silent retreat day three. The urge to talk is gone. Just footsteps and birds.
Lantern festival by the river. Thousands of little lights drifting. Everyone hushed.
My manager noticed I was struggling and gave me the week off, paid. No questions.
Appreciating my old school friends tonight. Twenty years and we still show up for each other.
The team threw me a surprise send-off. Speeches, a card everyone signed, Wendy cried. I didn't know I mattered this much here.
Thankful that the storm missed us. Thinking of the people on the coast who weren't so lucky.
Our elderly neighbour, Mrs. Kowalski, brought pierogi for the whole street after the power cut.
Zainab dropped off a lasagne and a pile of library books when she heard about the breakup. She didn't ask any questions.
Deeply thankful to the stranger who stopped and called the ambulance when I fainted. I never got his name.
Thankful for Thursday dinners with Arjun and Meera. Same curry place for six years.
The interpreter at the asylum hearing made sure every word I said was heard. I hugged her after.
Brigitte read every page of my draft and left notes in green pen. Kindest edit I've ever had.
Two hours on hold with the airline. Disconnected. Started again.
Same argument with Mum about the wedding guest list. Round five. Nobody wins.
Kids fought all the way to Grandma's. Four hours of 'he's touching me'. I have no patience left.
Spent the whole weekend on the furniture flatpack and there's one piece left over and the drawer won't close.
I'm not angry at Nkechi, I'm just frustrated that we keep having the same conversation about money and nothing changes.
Bureaucracy day: three offices, two forms, one stamp, zero progress.
Ma keeps sending me articles about 'settling down'. I'm 29. I have a life. I'm settled.
Rejected the visa on a technicality. A missing stamp. Months of waiting for this.
My research participant cancelled for the fourth time and the ethics deadline is next week.
Trying to get my dad to see a doctor about his cough. He just changes the subject.
Lost the bid by one vote. Three months of work. They picked the cheaper, worse plan.
The publisher wants to see the full manuscript. Not a yes yet but it's the closest I've ever been.
Moving into the new flat in nine days. Already measuring for shelves.
The grant is shortlisted! Final decision in a month. Trying not to plan the whole project in my head already. Failing.
Course starts in October and I've already read half the reading list. Nerd and proud.
Tomorrow I start learning to dive. Open water by the end of the week if the instructor, Mika, thinks I'm ready.
Seo-yeon just told me she's moving to my city! Pinch me.
Can't wait for Diwali at Nani's. Lamps, sweets, all the cousins in one house.
Dad is finally coming to visit me abroad. Planning everything I want to show him.
Got into the pottery residency in Kyoto!!! Leaving in May.
I'm going to be an aunt!!! Kezia told us at dinner and I screamed in a restaurant.
Funerals make you think. Listening to the speeches for Mr. Ito I wondered what people would say about me.
The argument with Jonas was about the dishes on the surface. Underneath it's about feeling unseen. Need to say that next time.
Journaling prompt: what am I tolerating? Answer: a job that drains me, a friendship that's one-sided, my own inner critic.
Birthday thoughts at 50: fewer things, more people, better shoes.
Thinking about how much of my personality is just my mother's anxieties in a nicer outfit.
What does enough look like? Enough money, enough work, enough approval. Trying to put a number on it.
Kieran asked what I'm proud of and I couldn't answer quickly. Thinking about that.
I see now that I was depressed that whole winter. Couldn't name it then. Can name it now.
I've realised I'm happiest when I'm making something with my hands. Should probably build my life around that.
I think I've confused being needed with being loved for a long time.
First green shoots on the plot after the long winter. Maybe this year the garden will actually work.
The ceasefire is holding. Called my cousins back home and for once they sounded light.
Lena called from rehab. She sounded clearer than I've heard her in two years.
My first therapy session was awkward and I cried the whole time. But Anja, the therapist, said 'we can work with this' and I believed her.
Marisol got the job interview she wanted. Helping her prepare. Feels like her luck is turning.
Mum's scan shows the tumour has shrunk. Long road still. But shrunk.
After months of no response, two companies want to talk next week. Something's moving.
Wrote one page today after six months of nothing. Maybe the writing is coming back.
The rescue dog let me pet her today. Took six weeks. She's learning that hands can be gentle.
Kids and I made a vision board for the summer: beach, picnics, bikes. Looking forward to every square of it.
Low energy all week. Probably the cold I can't shake.
Brain fog today. Read the same email five times.
Harvest season. Up at four every day, home at dark. Too tired to even shower properly.
Teething. Hers, not mine. Though at this point I'd believe either.
Ran the 6am bootcamp, then a full day at the office, then Tomasz's birthday drinks. Done for.
Insomnia again. Watched the ceiling until 5. Got up at 7. Everything feels far away.
Pulled an all-nighter for the deadline. Shipped it. Now I can barely string a sentence together.
Ward was understaffed. Twelve hours without a proper break. Came home and lay on the kitchen floor for a bit.
Dragged myself through the gym session. Zero energy. Probably should have rested.
Long day of meetings. Talked so much my face hurts. Brain is empty.
Lethargic. Did nothing all day. Even nothing felt like effort.
Found out Ray has been lying about where the money went. Two years of lying.
Watched the news about the factory dumping waste in the river and I'm genuinely enraged.
Uncle Desmond said something horrible about my wife at dinner and everyone laughed. I walked out.
Kerry-Ann's ex showed up at her work and made a scene. I wanted to throw him into the road.
Rage. My essay was plagiarised by someone in my class and he got the higher mark.
Absolutely incensed that the hospital lost Mum's test results. Again. She has to redo the whole thing.
Fumed the whole commute. The new policy means we lose our flexible hours with one week's notice.
Tradesman took the deposit and disappeared. £800.
The court let him off with a warning. A warning.
No big news. Kids are healthy, bills are paid, Aziz made his good curry. That's a full life.
Walked the same loop as always and still noticed new things. Life's good.
Our tenth anniversary. Takeaway on the floor of the living room like our first night here. Still happy with him.
Feeling at peace with where I am. Not the career I planned but a life I like.
Fridge full, house warm, everyone asleep. Good night.
Satisfied. That's the word for this week.
Everything in its place today. Inbox clear, house clean, dinner simmering. Lovely.
Pyjamas by 7, takeaway pizza, old sitcom. No regrets.
I've stopped wanting a bigger house. This one has everything we need.
Cooked a proper meal from scratch for the first time in weeks. Satisfying.
All the boxes ticked: workout done, vegetables eaten, called Gran, eight hours of sleep.
Since Harold died the evenings are the hardest. His chair, the empty side of the bed.
Wish I had a friend to go to the cinema with. Went alone. It was fine. Mostly.
Ordered takeaway just to talk to the delivery guy for a minute.
The only person who really got me was Nana and she's been gone a year today.
Watched couples at the beach and felt a pang. Not jealous exactly. Just alone.
Walked past our old café and Liv wasn't there, of course. She moved two years ago. Still look every time.
Feeling disconnected from everyone. Like I'm watching life through a window.
My son doesn't call much since he moved in with his girlfriend. I don't want to bother him.
I'm tired of being the one who reaches out. Stopped this week to see who notices. Nobody so far.
Even with Amira here this week I feel lonely. She's here but her mind is somewhere else.
My daughter stood up for a kid who was being picked on. The teacher called to tell me. I'm so proud of her.
Our team raised £12,000 for the hospice. Rhiannon cried when we announced the total.
Taught Grandma to video call. She called me four times to practise. Proud of us both.
Our little shop turned a profit for the first time. Framed the receipt.
Ran the meeting for the first time. Nobody noticed I was nervous. I think I'm good at this.
The kids cleaned their rooms without being asked. I must be doing something right.
Finished the quilt for Shanthi's baby. 200 hours of stitching. Every square has a meaning.
Our community garden opened today. Three years of meetings, petitions and digging. Councillor Ahmed cut the ribbon.
Henri performed his first stand-up set. Terrible jokes. Brave as anything. So proud.
Finished the hardest course of the degree with a distinction.
Too much. Everything at once. Sat on the bathroom floor for ten minutes just to breathe.
Renovation chaos. Dust everywhere, no kitchen, the builder hasn't turned up and the budget's gone.
So many decisions about Mum's care. Every option has a cost. I keep making spreadsheets and crying.
Christmas prep: gifts for 23 people, hosting, a work party, the school play. And it's only the 2nd.
Starting uni is a lot. Lectures, timetables, finding rooms, meeting people. My head is spinning.
Kids screaming, phone ringing, dinner burning, doorbell. All at once. I just stood there.
I said yes to too many things this month. Calendar is solid colour. No white space anywhere.
Teaching five classes, marking, parents' evening, inspection next week. Running on adrenaline and coffee.
Picking up three shifts plus the course plus helping Delia with the baby. My head is full of noise.
I keep forgetting things. Appointments, birthdays, why I walked into the room. Too much in my head.
Not a bad day, just too full. Back-to-back from 7am to 10pm.
Dentist at 10. Groceries after. Picked up the dry cleaning.
Called the plumber about the radiator. He's coming on Thursday between 8 and 12.
Doctor's appointment for the annual check-up. Blood pressure normal. Next check in a year.
Team stand-up at 9:30. Pairing with Rohan on the API migration in the afternoon.
Cooked a big batch of chilli for the week. Froze four portions.
Swapped shifts with Olivia so I can do the Tuesday early. Confirmed with the rota manager.
Visited the new Ikea with Kostas. Bought a lamp and some storage boxes.
Spent the day cataloguing the archive boxes. Boxes 14 to 22 done.
Got a haircut. Same style. Paid £18.
Bank holiday. Stayed home. Did some reading and a bit of gardening.
Wonderful, Simon 'forgot' to book the venue. Very cool of him, two days before the party.
I'm not even angry anymore about the lie. Just disappointed and quiet.
I wouldn't say I'm happy about the move. But I'm not dreading it anymore either. Somewhere in the middle.
Got the results: distinction. Wanted to call Grandpa first like always. Then remembered. Sat on the stairs holding the letter.
I keep laughing at Ollie's jokes on the phone and then crying after I hang up. Long distance is weird.
By 2030 I want to have my own studio. Wrote it down today so it's real.
I keep reorganising the spice rack instead of opening the letter from the court.
Made his favourite dinner and set two plates before I remembered.

Today was the day I finally went back to the climbing wall after the fall. I'd been avoiding it for four months, telling myself I was busy, telling Sol I'd lost interest, telling myself the wrist still hurt when it really didn't. I stood at the bottom of the easiest route for a long time. My hands were sweating so much I had to chalk them three times. The first few moves were fine. Then at the point where I fell last time I froze, and the old panic came up my throat. I breathed. I looked at my feet. I made the move. I got to the top of a route a child could climb and I sat at the top crying a bit. Sol was below grinning. I'm so proud of myself I could burst.

Sunday, and the whole family came for lunch for the first time since Nonna's funeral. I was worried it would be sad, that we'd all sit around her empty chair and not know what to say. Instead Zio Franco told the story about Nonna chasing the priest out of the kitchen with a wooden spoon, and everyone laughed until they cried, and then just cried, and then laughed again. My niece Bianca made the gnocchi using Nonna's recipe and they were lumpy and perfect. We stayed at the table until it was dark. Nobody wanted to clear the plates. Driving home I felt full in every sense, grateful that we still have each other and still have her, in the stories and the recipes and the noise.

I'm writing this on the train back from the hospital and I'm so angry I can barely hold the pen. They discharged Dad yesterday even though he could hardly stand, because they 'needed the bed'. No care plan, no follow-up, a bag of pills and a leaflet. Last night he fell in the bathroom and lay there for two hours before the neighbour heard him. Now he's back in A&E with a fractured hip and the same doctor who discharged him is acting like it's bad luck. It isn't bad luck. It's a system that treats old people like parcels. I made a formal complaint and the woman at the desk sighed at me like I was the problem. I wanted to scream at someone and there was nobody to scream at who deserved it.

Today I told my parents I'm not going to do the law degree. I'd planned the conversation for weeks. I chose the moment carefully, after dinner, after Dad's second cup of tea. I explained about the design course, the portfolio, the scholarship I've already applied for. Mum went very quiet. Dad said 'we'll talk about it later' and turned on the television. That was it. No shouting, which I'd prepared for, but no support either. I'm sitting in my room now feeling sick and stubborn in equal measure. I know I'm right. I know it's my life. I just wish knowing you're right felt better than this. I don't know if they'll come round. I'm going to go anyway.
A strange, floaty day. Like being in between two versions of myself.
Mrs. Kaur's grandson, the one who plays violin, gave a concert in the community hall. Mrs. Kaur glowed all evening.
Saw 'The Fall of Rome' at the theatre with Gwen. Three hours. Gwen slept for one of them.
Oh good, the cat was sick on my laptop. Productivity unlocked.
What a joy, a 6am fire alarm drill in December. Everyone in pyjamas in the snow.
Haven't cried once since the funeral. People seem to expect it. I just feel numb.
Wasn't expecting much from the blind date. Turns out Kofi is hilarious and we talked until the café closed.
